verses.text: Listen, Israel! Today you are about to cross the Jordan River to take over the land of nations bigger and stronger than you, with large cities that have walls reaching up to the sky.
The people are strong and tall. They are the Anakites. You know about them, and you have heard it said, "Who can stand up against the Anakites?"

But be sure of this today: the LORD your God is the one who goes across ahead of you like a fire that burns everything up. He will destroy them and bring them down before you. You will drive them out and wipe them out quickly, as the LORD promised you.

After the LORD your God has driven them out ahead of you, do not say to yourself, "The LORD brought me here to take this land because I am so good." No, it is because these nations are so wicked that the LORD is driving them out ahead of you.

You are not going in to take their land because you are good or because your heart is honest. It is because these nations are wicked that the LORD your God will drive them out ahead of you, and to keep the promise he made to your ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
So understand that the LORD your God is not giving you this good land to own because you are good. In fact, you are a stubborn people.
Remember, and never forget, how you made the LORD your God angry in the desert. From the day you left Egypt until you arrived here, you have kept rebelling against the LORD.
Even at Mount Sinai you made the LORD so angry that he was ready to destroy you.

I had gone up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant the LORD had made with you. I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I did not eat any food or drink any water.
The LORD gave me two stone tablets written by the finger of God. On them were all the words the LORD spoke to you on the mountain out of the fire, on the day you were all gathered there.
At the end of the forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

Then the LORD said to me, "Get up and go down from here at once, because your people whom you brought out of Egypt have become evil. They have quickly turned away from what I commanded them and have made a metal idol for themselves!"
The LORD also said to me, "I have seen these people, and they are very stubborn.
Leave me alone so that I can destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation stronger and bigger than they are."
So I turned and went down the mountain while it was blazing with fire. The two tablets of the covenant were in my hands.
When I looked, I saw that you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made yourselves an idol shaped like a calf. You had quickly turned away from the way the LORD had commanded you.
So I took the two tablets and threw them down from my hands, breaking them in front of your eyes.

Then once again I lay face down before the LORD for forty days and forty nights. I did not eat any food or drink any water, because of all the sin you had done, doing what was evil in the LORD's sight and making him angry.
I was afraid of the LORD's terrible anger, because he was angry enough to destroy you. But again the LORD listened to me.
The LORD was also angry enough with Aaron to destroy him, but at that time I prayed for Aaron too.
Then I took that sinful calf you had made and burned it in the fire. I crushed it and ground it into powder as fine as dust, and threw the dust into the stream that flowed down the mountain.
You also made the LORD angry at Taberah, at Massah, and at Kibroth Hattaavah.

And when the LORD sent you out from Kadesh Barnea, he said, "Go up and take over the land I have given you." But you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God. You did not trust him or obey him.
You have been rebelling against the LORD ever since I have known you.
So I lay face down before the LORD for those forty days and forty nights, because the LORD had said he would destroy you.
I prayed to the LORD and said, "Lord GOD, do not destroy your people, your own special people, whom you rescued by your great power and brought out of Egypt with your mighty hand.
Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not look at how stubborn these people are, or at their wickedness and sin.

Otherwise the people of the land you brought us out of will say, 'The LORD was not able to take them into the land he promised them, and he hated them. So he brought them out to kill them in the desert.'
But they are your people, your own special people, whom you brought out by your great power and your mighty arm."
